newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Huey Tai increases convertible bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Huey Tai increases convertible bond issue.

text.p: Huey Tai International Ltd said it would increase the size of its planned US$50 million convertible bond issue by US$8.0 million in an agreement with the issuer signed last week.
The additional US$8.0 million will be issued solely to cover over-allotment, Huey Tai said in a notice published on Monday.
The convertible bonds are issued at par, carry a coupon rate of 6.5 percent and are due in 2000.
The bonds will pay interest semi-annually in arrears on February 11 and August 11.

The bonds will carry a right to convert into shares at an initial conversion price of HK$1.75 per share, a premium of 3.73 percent over the average closing of the shares for 10 dealing days ended February 4, and with a fixed rate of exchange on conversion of US$1.00 equal to HK$7.75015, the notice said.

Assuming the full conversion of the bonds into shares, excluding the over-allotment option, at the initial conversion price, the company will issue 221.43 million new shares, representing approximately 16.94 percent of existing issued share capital and 14.49 percent of the enlarged share capital.
If the over-allotment is exercised, the company will issue 256.86 million new shares representing 16.42 percent of the enlarged issued capital.

The net proceeds of the issued of approximately US$48.45 million, or US$56.25 million if the over-allotment is exercised in full, will be used for general working capital and general corporate purposes, the notice said.
The issue is being arranged and lead managed by CEF Capital Ltd. Huey Tai closed at HK$1.75 on February 5, the last day of trading before the start of the Chinese Lunar New Year holidays.
